conceptual assets.information: The four 32-bit XTEA key words stored in key_mem are used by the cryptographic computation and can be read through the CSR interface.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The key is exposed by the CSR readback at csr_rdata_o (185), and CSR writes can replace key_mem contents (178-179).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read csr_rdata_o to recover the key or write replacement words through the CSR interface to cause incorrect XTEA results.

conceptual assets.information: The rs1_i and rs2_i words form the operand data captured for an XTEA operation; the computation depends on them to derive the returned result. The operands do not leave the unit whole.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The operand values are captured into xtea.opa and xtea.opb (205-206), and operand-dependent computation is exposed through result_o (222-224,249), while changing the input values changes the cryptographic result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe operand-dependent output or replace rs1_i or rs2_i before capture to disclose or corrupt the processed data.

conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit XTEA result produced in xtea.res is returned to the processor through result_o. The cryptographic operation depends on this value being correct and available.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: result_o exposes xtea.res (222,224,249), the result is computed from operands and key material (222-224,238), and result selection can withhold or replace it with zero when the operation is not valid (250-262).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the operands or key to corrupt the result, observe the returned cryptographic data, or prevent a valid result from being presented.

conceptual assets.information: The done pipeline in xtea.done records the progress and completion timing of an XTEA operation and controls when valid_o reports completion. It is generated internally rather than carried in through a data port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Clocked assignments update xtea.done and its state controls valid_o (200-207,250), so corruption can make completion occur at the wrong time or prevent a valid result from being released.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could disturb the progress state or its launch condition so that the operation reports an invalid result or never reports completion.

conceptual assets.information: start_i requests capture of the operands and launch of an XTEA operation; the unit depends on this command to begin processing.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The start command controls operand capture and sets the operation-progress state (204-207), so changing or suppressing it can cause an unintended operation or prevent processing from starting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress start_i to block XTEA operations or assert it at an unintended time to process the wrong operand values.

conceptual assets.information: The CSR write-enable and word-address command determines whether key_mem is written and which key word is selected for writing or readback.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: csr_we_i gates key updates and csr_addr_i selects the addressed key word (178-179), while csr_addr_i also selects the readback word (185), allowing unauthorized suppression or redirection of key access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter csr_we_i or csr_addr_i to suppress key programming, redirect a write to another key word, or prevent the intended cryptographic configuration.

considered, not kept.reason: rtype_i and funct3_i only select the operation or result form, so the Operation selectors rule makes them part of the operation rather than a separate conceptual asset (204,213-225,245-256).
active_i, funct7_i and rs3_i are never read or used by the RTL, so this unit does not use them as information requiring a security objective (26,35,38).
